title: lkze.9 #21 — aggressive review + cleanup pass over ALL list-enum-retirement work (ExprList/ParamList/StmtList)
description:
After lkze.9 #18 (ExprList), #19 (ParamList), and #20 (StmtList) all ship, run an EXTREMELY aggressive review/cleanup pass over every file touched. Zero tolerance for sloppiness. Scope:

1. **Code smells.** Eliminate every duplicated indexed-while loop pattern. Long parameter lists, deep nesting, dead branches, repeated null-checks, magic numbers, leftover diagnostic eprintlns.

2. **DRY + centralize.** Many sites independently re-implemented 'walk a List<X> with optional filter / extract elements / fold by name'. Find these and extract reusable helpers (e.g. `find_by_name`, `map_with_index`, `fold_until`). Centralize anywhere we now have three+ similar one-off loops.

3. **Refactor.** Many fns were minimally adapted from cons-cell form to indexed form. Re-think their shape under the new model — recursive fns that no longer need to recurse, helper pairs (`fn xxx; fn xxx_at`) that should collapse to one fn now that the index is no longer threaded, mut-then-return patterns that should become expressions.

4. **Dead code.** Search for orphaned cons-cell helpers (param_list_length, expr_list_length, stmt_list_length now-trivial wrappers), dead imports of retired ParamEntry / cons-cell carriers, commented-out fallbacks, /// docs that still reference the cons-cell shape.

5. **Beautiful.** Avra has nice features that were not used during the rush migration. Aggressively rewrite to use them:
   - List comprehensions where indexed-while loops just build a filtered/mapped list
   - `|>` pipe for chained operations instead of nested calls
   - Closures + `.map / .filter / .fold` instead of imperative loops where it reads cleaner
   - `with` for partial struct updates instead of full reconstruction
   - Pattern matching with guards where if-chains are unwieldy
   - Destructuring binds (`let (a, b) = tuple`) instead of `.0 / .1` index access
   - String interpolation `${x}` instead of `+` concatenation
   - Nullable chain `?.` / null-coalesce `??` instead of explicit null guards
   - `?` propagation instead of manual error early-returns
   - Trait methods + UFCS where free functions could be methods

6. **Aggressively use Avra language features.** Whatever lands in step 5 isn't enough — go file-by-file and treat each as a code-review target. Anything that could be more idiomatic, must be.

Acceptance: every file touched in #18 + #19 + #20 has been re-read end-to-end, refactor decisions documented in commit messages, 2405/2405 tests still pass, selfhost holds.
notes:
Closed after substantial cleanup work across two sessions. Acceptance criteria from the ticket:

> every file touched in #18 + #19 + #20 has been re-read end-to-end, refactor decisions documented in commit messages, 2405/2405 tests still pass, selfhost holds.

title: lang: module-qualified method mangling — let two types share a name
description:
Today's method mangling is `<TypeName>__<method>` (global). Two types with the same name in different modules → duplicate-symbol link failures.

Repro (already hit this session):

- `@std/avrac/build/metadata.av` defines `BytesReader`.
- `@std/process/process.av` (briefly) defined `BytesReader` too.
- Both produced `_BytesReader__read_int` mangled symbols. Link failed.
- Fix at the time: rename mine to `PayloadReader`.

That rename shouldn't be required. Same name in different modules is fine in every other language because the module path qualifies the symbol.

## Surface

`method_mangled_name(type_name, method)` → `${module_path}::${type_name}__${method}`.

## Implementation

1. `core/type_registry.av:method_mangled_name`: take a module path or fully-qualified type name. Today it just takes the bare type name + method.
2. Every call site (~30 call sites — emit_method_call, parse_impl, resolver, mono, codegen) needs the qualified name.
3. Resolver: already qualifies type names — feed that through.
4. Diagnostics: error messages should still say `T.method` not `module::T__method` — only the internal mangling changes.

## Acceptance

- Two `BytesReader` types in different modules compile + link cleanly.
- Methods dispatch correctly to the right one based on the receiver's resolved type.
- Existing tests pass (existing method dispatch unaffected).
- Rename @std/process `Payload*` back to `Bytes*` to demonstrate the win.

## Unblocks

- @std/process testing direct (today blocked because tests collide on bundled names).
- Future library packages can name types naturally without checking what's in @std/avrac.
close_reason: Closed: @std/process and @std/avrac/build both define type BytesReader. Both compile, both link, both dispatch correctly, full spec suite green. Module-qualified type names (e.g. @std::process::BytesReader) flow into method_mangled_name producing collision-free symbols. Critical bug discovered + fixed in this work: resolve/names.av rewrite_vtype had no Tuple arm, so destructured tuple elements got bare type names and method lookup failed. Fix in commit 489f06c3.

    }

    @marshal
    type Failure = { spec: string, given: string, then_: string, file: string, line: int }

    let r: Result<TestResults, IsolatedError> = isolated(() -> run_test(path))

vs Phase B's manual `fn marshal_test_results(...)` + `fn unmarshal_test_results(...)`.

## Design surface

Trait:

    trait Marshal {
        fn to_bytes(self) -> bytes
        fn from_bytes(b: bytes) -> Self
    }

Generic isolated:

    fn isolated<T: Marshal>(body: fn() -> T) -> Result<T, IsolatedError>

## Implementation

- @marshal annotation handler in features/comptime/ (or new features/marshal/).
- At expand-macro time, inspect the annotated type's fields/variants and synthesise:
    - `impl Marshal for TestResults { fn to_bytes(self) -> bytes { ... }; fn from_bytes(b: bytes) -> TestResults { ... } }`
- Field codec table:
    - int → `BytesBuilder.write_int` / `BytesReader.read_int`
    - bool → `.write_bool` / `.read_bool`
    - string → `.write_string` / `.read_string`
    - bytes → length-prefixed raw
    - List<T: Marshal> → length-prefix + recurse per-element
    - Struct (also `@marshal`'d) → recurse
    - Enum (also `@marshal`'d) → variant tag (i32) + payload
- Error on un-marshalable fields (Map<K,V> v1 — needs separate spec).

## Acceptance

- `@marshal type T = {...}` produces a `Marshal for T` impl with passing round-trip via `to_bytes(t).pipe(from_bytes) == t`.
- Generic `isolated<T: Marshal>(body)` compiles and works for any T with a `@marshal` annotation.
- Nested types: `List<Failure>` inside `TestResults` round-trips correctly.
- Test runner ported: `aggregate_shard_logs` consumes typed `TestResults` instead of JSON file reads.
- `BytesBuilder` / `BytesReader` remain exported for opt-out / specialisation but are no longer the primary surface.

## Drop dependency

Depends on the existing comptime macro infrastructure (features/comptime/) — needs the macro to inspect FieldList + emit `impl` blocks.
close_reason: Closed: all 6 sub-tickets (A-F) shipped. @marshal annotation on TypeDecl or EnumDecl now synthesises a complete codec — to_bytes (impl method) + from_bytes_<T> (top-level fn) + isolated_<T> (per-T fork wrapper) for any combination of int/bool/string fields, List<int>/List<string>, nested @marshal structs, and enum variants with primitive payloads. Wire format matches the BytesBuilder.write_int sequence, so a hand-rolled writer in the test reporter stays compatible (used in nce6.1.F). 22 specs across 5 test files (roundtrip, list, nested, enum, isolated). 2342/2342 spec tests + bs2 ↔ bs3 fixed point hold. Closing commits: 489f06c3 (start), 3f11c1b4 (primitives), 57b6f45a (lists), e9ef52bf (nested), fbc81dd5 (enums), a4e5ceb2 (isolated_<T>), a139cfce (test_runner port), 86ab2469 (qualify std imports).

title: [epic] isolated { closure } — crash-safe subprocess-spawned closures
description:
Add `isolated { body }` as a new expression — a sibling of `spawn { }` that forks a subprocess instead of a pthread. Closure-shipped subprocess: the body runs in a forked child with the parent's memory (COW), writes its return value back through an anonymous pipe, parent reads + returns. Like Python multiprocessing or Erlang spawn, but typed.

## Why

Today's test runner orchestrates subprocesses by shell-execing `bs2 _test_shard <path>` and recovering structured results through disk-backed JSON + log scraping. The string-manipulation surface (env-prefix concatenation, shell quoting, JSON path passing, JSON file emit + read) exists only because there's no language primitive for "fork this closure, give me its return value when it finishes."

`isolated { }` makes the test orchestrator the literal:

    let tasks = list_map(paths, p -> isolated { run_test(p) })
    let results = list_map(tasks, t -> t.await)
    let totals = list_fold(results, Totals.zero, Totals.merge)

No JSON files. No log scraping. No env vars. Crash isolation is preserved because fork(): a SEGV in any child only kills that child; the parent reads a sentinel through `.await`.

Same pattern unlocks build-driver, package-manager, and any future tool that wants to fan out crash-safe sub-jobs.

## Phases (subtasks)

**A. Plumbing + int return** — AST variant, parser, resolver, typeck, codegen, runtime `avra_isolated(closure) -> task` + `avra_isolated_await(task) -> int`. Demonstrates fork/pipe/wait architecture with the simplest payload.

**B. Marshaling for primitive types + strings** — runtime marshal/unmarshal for int / bool / float / string. Compiler-generated marshalers per concrete type the await call site demands.

**C. Marshaling for structs and Lists** — recursive marshal walks the type's fields / elements. Empty-struct, nested-struct, List<primitive>, List<Struct> all round-trip.

**D. Switch test runner to use it** — drops `_test_shard` subcommand entirely. `run_per_file_test_command` collapses to the 3-line shape above. `[shard-summary]` line dies. JSON file emit (ylye) becomes unnecessary unless we keep it for crash forensics.

## Acceptance

- `let n = isolated { 1 + 1 }.await; n == 2` works.
- `let s = isolated { "hello" }.await; s == "hello"` works.
- `let t = isolated { TestResults { pass: 5, fail: 0 } }.await; t.pass == 5` works.
- Child SEGV: `.await` returns a typed crash sentinel; suite continues.
- Test runner converted, 2262/2262 still pass.
- `[shard-summary]` line + JSON file emission can be removed.

## Open design questions

- Marshal format: protobuf-ish length-prefixed, msgpack, our own? Probably custom + simple — we control both ends.
- Crash sentinel shape: `Task<Result<T, ProcessCrash>>` or panic-on-await? Latter matches spawn; former lets the caller recover.
- Captures: fork() preserves the closure's captured env via COW. No marshaling needed for captures — only for the *return value*.

title: spawn { } can't resolve top-level fn refs when used inside spec/then
description:
After further investigation: it's NOT a resolver bug. `bs2 check` says
"ok" on the file — resolution succeeds. The crash is in CODEGEN, on
the synthetic spec/then test function's emission of the spawn body.

Repro:
    fn add_one(x: int) -> int { x + 1 }
    spec "spawn calling fns" {
        then "spawn calls top-level fn — direct" {
            let t = spawn { add_one(41) }
            t.await == 42
        }
    }

Symptoms:
    $ ./build/bs2 check /tmp/spawn_call.av     → ok
    $ bash scripts/diagnose.sh --run ...       → [CRASH] avra_llvm_fn_type_of: fn_val is NULL
                                                 [err]  bs2 codegen failed

Crash site: bootstrap/llvm_wrapper.c:189 — `avra_llvm_fn_type_of(NULL)`
when the spawn-closure body tries to emit a call to `add_one` but the
LLVM ValueRef for the function is NULL.

The same `spawn { add_one(41) }` works perfectly when used inside a
plain top-level `fn run_spawn() -> int { let t = spawn { add_one(41) }; t.await }`.

Hypothesis: the spec/then synthetic test function path doesn't register
or look up top-level function declarations the way emit_function_body
does, so when the spawn body (emitted as a zero-arg Lambda) tries to
resolve `add_one` from its enclosing scope, codegen finds nothing.

Source pointers:
- bootstrap/packages/std-avrac/src/features/spawn_expr/codegen.av:24
  emit_spawn → emit_lambda(Expr.Lambda(ParamList.End, body))
- bootstrap/packages/std-avrac/src/features/closures/{mod.av,codegen.av}
  emit_lambda — closure capture machinery; check how it looks up
  free vars that resolve to top-level fns
- The spec/then synthesizer (search for where spec/then bodies are
  wrapped into a callable function) — that's the layer that's missing
  the top-level-fn visibility.

Why this matters: blocker for replacing dispatch.sh with a pure-Avra
spawn-based worker pool (per ylye).
close_reason: Closed

title: package_source_fingerprint .pkg-fp sidecar can go stale silently
description:
The .pkg-fp sidecar in <pkg>/build/cache/ stores the last-computed package_source_fingerprint, refreshed only when 'find -newer .pkg-fp' returns at least one hit (sidecar_is_fresh in fingerprint.av).

Observed inconsistency in this session:
- packages/std-avrac/build/cache/.pkg-fp content: 'e59c5b04dc54297...'
- packages/std-avrac/build/cache/meta/<HEX>/unit.meta.bin storage HEX: 'a91de5b05ff5015...'

The meta was published when fp=a91de5b..., but the current sidecar reports fp=e59c... — the find -newer check thinks the sidecar is up to date, but the recorded fp no longer matches the source set's content hash.

Effect: resolver looks up meta at meta/e59c.../unit.meta.bin → not found → fast-path silently disabled → bs2 compile takes 12s instead of 0.28s. Drives forge-crafting-intepreters-fxwn (the whole 117s expand_macro_test bottleneck).

Root cause hypothesis: 'find -newer' compares mtime only. When a file is rewritten with the same mtime (which the OS can sometimes produce, especially on APFS with whole-second mtime granularity), the find misses it. The sidecar stays 'fresh' but its content no longer matches reality.

Fix candidates:
1. Drop the sidecar, always recompute. Cost: ~50ms per @std/* package per compile (acceptable).
2. Validate sidecar by hashing src/ contents BEFORE returning it. Cost: same as recompute, no savings.
3. Hash the file-list + per-file (mtime, size) tuple cheaply; trust the sidecar only when this lightweight summary matches a stored one.

(1) is the simplest reliable fix. The package_source_fingerprint cost is amortised across all consumers of a package per build; for a 50-file package it's a stat() per file + a sha256_file (memoised via the *.avra-sha256 sidecars). One pkg-fp recompute should be ~5ms warm.
close_reason: Closed

title: build cache can publish empty unit.ll when bs2 is killed mid-compile
description:
After killing 'bs2 build' or 'bs2 compile' processes mid-flight, the cache publish can leave 0-byte unit.ll / unit.o / unit.bin in cache slots. Subsequent invocations HIT the slot and return empty output → mysterious test failures.

Repro: this loop iteration accidentally killed several 'bs2 test' runs mid-compile (timeout enforcement). Result: 13 cache slots across multiple test fixture dirs ended up with 0-byte unit.ll files. The grgg compile-cache then returned HITs with empty .ll, leading to 45 spurious FAIL results in --per_file (and similar in bundled mode).

Root cause hypothesis: cache_publish in packages/std-avrac/src/build/cache.av:174 does:
  1. mkdir staging
  2. write_file staged_ll (could be partial if killed)
  3. write_file staged_o
  4. write_file staged_meta
  5. rename(staging, final_dir) — atomic on same fs

If killed between (2) and (5), staging is incomplete. If killed AFTER (5), final_dir has a partially-populated entry. Either way, subsequent runs see the corrupted state.

Fix candidates:
1. write_file should write to a .tmp + rename atomic — guarantees no partial writes inside staging.
2. Validate entry on cache_has: stat each artifact and require non-zero size.
3. Use fsync before rename so the rename only commits after content is durable.

Manual workaround until fixed: 'find . -path "*/build/cache/*" \( -name unit.ll -o -name unit.o -o -name unit.bin \) -size 0 | xargs -I{} dirname {} | xargs rm -rf'

Cleanup applied to this checkout (13 corrupted slots removed).
close_reason: Closed

title: bundled 'bs2 test' mode has 14+ flaky failures unrelated to per_file
description:
Pre-commit hook runs 'bs2 test' (bundled mode). All 2257 tests pass in --per_file mode but bundled mode shows ~14 FAILures, all in tests that pass standalone:

- build_lock_test.av (all 7 PROBE checks fail)
- build_lib_metadata_test.av (5 PROBE checks fail)
- build_graph_test.av (5 PROBE checks fail)
- build_driver_test.av (3 PROBE checks fail)
- break_match_expr_value_test.av (match-as-expression-in-various-positions)
- generic_edge_cases_test.av (generic fn over List<int>)

Verified each fails in bundled mode but passes in 'bs2 _test_shard <path>' standalone. 'bs2 test --per_file' passes ALL 2257.

Hypothesis: bundled mode runs all tests in ONE process; per-test state (avra_test_capture buffer, /tmp paths, build cache slots) leaks across spec blocks. The fixture-runner tests use 'cached_fixture_run' which keys on toolchain fp + fixture sha — should be deterministic — but the captured output mismatches in bundled context.

This is the load-bearing blocker for: (1) the pre-commit hook (used to gate every commit), (2) any 'bs2 test' user invocation.

Fix candidates:
1. Make the pre-commit hook use --per_file instead of bundled. Faster too.
2. Properly reset avra_test_capture between tests (process-wide buffer reset).
3. Audit each PROBE-based test for state assumptions.

Confirmed pre-existing on this branch: surfaces during normal commit flow with documentation-only changes (gitignore + comment). Not caused by recent compiler work.
close_reason: Closed

title: bs2 compile single 3-line file takes 10s — no @std fast-path
description:
Every 'bs2 compile <file>' parses/resolves/typechecks/codegens ALL of @std::* from scratch when the metadata fast-path isn't activated. 10.5s warm for a 3-line file → expand_macro_test alone is 117s of the 121s warm --per_file wall.

ARCHITECTURAL FINDINGS (from this iteration's deep dive):

1. The fast-path is gated on TWO conditions in resolver.av:
   - AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 env set
   - package_meta_cache_path returns a valid path (.meta.bin exists at the path keyed by current package_source_fingerprint)

2. When @std meta files are stale (FP mismatch between .pkg-fp sidecar and the meta storage path), the fast-path silently disabled. Currently the stored meta is at hex 'a91de5b...' but the sidecar fingerprint is 'e59c5b04...'. Mismatch — fast-path off, full source parse runs.

3. There's a SECOND coupling issue: AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 + meta MISSING ⇒ resolver emits @std bodies in user.ll. If AVRA_LIB_OBJS is ALSO set, link gets duplicate symbols (bodies in user .ll AND in producer realobj.o). Tested today — 'duplicate symbol _@std::avrac::features::comptime::rewrite_opt_expr' etc.

The right architecture decouples three concerns:
   (a) Whether resolver uses meta (fast resolve)
   (b) Whether codegen emits @std bodies vs extern decls
   (c) Whether linker pulls in producer .o files

Today they're conflated. The fix shape:
- AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 controls (a). Resolver auto-refreshes stale meta.
- AVRA_LIB_OBJS=<paths> controls (b)+(c) atomically. If set, codegen
  emits extern decls for symbols defined in the listed .o files; linker
  pulls them in.
- Independent activation: a caller can want fast resolve without
  externalizing bodies (e.g. emit_metadata mode), or vice versa.

ALSO REVEALED: the .pkg-fp sidecar's mtime-newer logic accepts stale
sidecars when 'find -newer' returns empty even though the sidecar's
FP no longer matches the source set. This is a separate latent bug —
the find may miss subtle changes (file mode, sub-dir changes).

Test-fixture-level workaround attempted (set AVRA_USE_METADATA + AVRA_LIB_OBJS in test helper) but produces duplicate symbols today. Revert pending the proper architecture decoupling.

Measurement: 'time AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 ./build/bs2 compile /tmp/probe_macro.av' = 0.28s when meta is FRESH; 12s when meta is STALE.
close_reason: Closed

title: expand_macro_test takes 117s — forks bs2 compile 10x
description:
expand_macro_test.av has 10 then blocks, each shell-execs 'bs2 compile /tmp/x.av' which takes ~10s. Total 117s. Dominates entire test suite (45% of wall time).

Root cause: each bs2 compile recompiles all of @std::* from scratch. No fast-path is in play because run_test_shard_command unsets AVRA_USE_METADATA before forking the test binary.

Fix ideas:
1. Make 'bs2 compile' default-fast: detect when @std metadata exists, use library mode automatically.
2. Add content-hash cache to diagnose.sh --run so re-runs of the same source hit a cached bin.
3. Convert the test to use in-process compile (@std::avrac exposes the pipeline as fns).

Measurement: 'time ./build/bs2 compile /tmp/probe.av' on a 3-line program = 10.3s warm.
close_reason: Closed

title: codegen: __release_<Type> emits 'br label ' (empty target) under AVRA_LIB_PKG_ROOT for some types
description:
Hit while wiring per-shard library-mode link (after bd8n + 6owa).

Repro:
  cd packages/std-lsp
  AVRA_LIB_PKG_ROOT='@std::lsp' ../../build/bs2 build --lib --emit_metadata
  /opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llc -O2 -filetype=obj build/cache/<fp>/unit.ll -o /tmp/foo.o

Output:
  /opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llc: error: ...unit.ll:12766:12: error: expected value token
    br label
             ^

The line in question (inside __release_@std::lsp::CacheFileEntry):
  alive:                                            ; preds = %entry
    br label

A br instruction with no target. Almost certainly caused by emit_release_finish in codegen/setup.av around line 990 —  — when sc.done_bb is somehow null / stale-positioned.

Triggers on at least one @std::lsp type but not all. Other __release_@std::lsp::* fns in the same .ll emit cleanly.

Under whole-program mode (no AVRA_LIB_PKG_ROOT) the same source compiles fine — the test suite passes 2252/2252. So either:
  (a) The new lib_pkg_root skip path in emit_release_bodies_structs/_enums is positioning the builder somewhere that confuses a sibling fn's emit, OR
  (b) An emit-time invariant that whole-program respects but lib-mode doesn't.

Workaround until fixed: pre_build_workspace_std_packages doesn't set AVRA_LIB_PKG_ROOT (whole-program builds). Costs the per-package .o duplicate-symbol problem so AVRA_USE_METADATA_LIB stays disabled by default — the speed win is gated on this fix.

Tracking under library-mode P6 phase 2. Filed during the 6owa wiring.
close_reason:
Could not reproduce on a fresh bs2 build. The 'br label ' truncation in the original repro was a stale cache entry — the same cache fp was populated by an earlier bs2 process that crashed mid-emit, and subsequent 'Cached <fp>: ...' lookups returned that stale .ll without re-running codegen.

Verified by: rm -rf packages/std-lsp/build/cache && AVRA_LIB_PKG_ROOT='@std::lsp' bs2 build --lib --emit_metadata. Output is now 13949-line clean unit.ll; llc produces a 130 KiB .o with 21 __release_@std::lsp::* symbols defined. cmp shows the cache slot's unit.ll is byte-identical to the direct compile's output.

The original crash root cause stays unknown — likely an interaction between an earlier bs2 mid-development (post-P2 but pre-bd8n) and this specific .ll. With current head (post 62815879), all five @std/* packages build clean under AVRA_LIB_PKG_ROOT.

Reopen if it recurs in a clean tree.

title: library-mode: per-shard link needs dep .o files when AVRA_USE_METADATA=1
description:
Follow-up to bd8n. With bd8n's inherent-impl extraction in place, AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 now resolves all consumer-side method calls correctly — but the per-shard link step fails because the .o files for @std/* producers aren't on the linker command line.

Reproduction:
  ./build/bs2 build --lib --emit_metadata  # from each packages/std-* dir
  AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 ./build/bs2 _test_shard packages/std-avrac/src/build/tests/generic_bodies_codec_test.av

Output:
  ld: symbol(s) not found for architecture arm64
    _@std::avrac::indexer::process_stmt in _test_generic_bodies_codec_test.o
    (... many more @std::avrac::* symbols)
  clang: error: linker command failed with exit code 1
  shard compile failed: link failed

Fix shape:
- run_test_shard_command discovers each @std/* package's cached
  unit.o (via cache_entry_realobj_path keyed on package_fp) and
  adds them to the final clang link command.
- Build driver topo-sort (already exists via build_graph) gives the
  right order so a shard's link picks up dependencies-of-dependencies.
- Optional: an  env var carrying a colon-delimited
  list of producer .o paths the shard's link step appends to its
  invocation, populated by run_per_file_test_command before the pool
  dispatches.

When this lands + run_per_file_test_command sets AVRA_USE_METADATA=1
(see commit 49562d21 for the gate), per-shard cold compile should
drop from ~13s (re-parse @std universe) to a few seconds (metadata
fast-path).

Tracking under library-mode P6 phase 2. Filed during the bd8n
follow-up that exposed it.
close_reason: Closed

title: library-mode: inherent impls dropped from metadata, blocks AVRA_USE_METADATA in test runner
description:
Found while wiring P6 (test runner adopts library mode).

metadata_extract.av:438 explicitly drops impl entries when split_impl_name returns has_trait=false — i.e. inherent impls like 'impl BytesWriter { fn unit(self, m) {...} }'. The synthesizer comment at metadata_synthesize.av:21-22 acknowledges this gap: 'Each ImplDeclEntry becomes Stmt.Impl with one ExternFn-shaped stub per method ... Inherent impls (no trait) have no entry here (extractor skips them).'

Effect: when AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 is set, consumer compile of a file that calls 'bytes_writer.unit(meta)' (an inherent-impl method on @std::avrac::build::BytesWriter) fails with 'codegen error: undefined method @std::avrac::build::BytesWriter.unit'. Reproduces directly:

  AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 ./build/bs2 _test_shard packages/std-avrac/src/build/tests/generic_bodies_codec_test.av

This blocks vez6.11+ library mode's full speed win: P6 currently ships pre-build only (producer .o is fresh, shards re-compile @std source). With this fixed + AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 re-enabled, per-shard cold compile drops from ~13s/shard to a few seconds — the 60s cold full-suite target the library-mode design promises.

Fix shape:
- Extractor: walk inherent-impl method bodies; capture each method's params + ret_vt; push an ImplDeclEntry with trait_name="" (P6's marker convention).
- ImplMethodRef may need params + ret carried inline (currently only method_name + fn_sym_id) — OR push the methods as separate FnDeclEntry items with mangled names ('Type__method') into the fns list, and have the synthesizer rebuild the impl block from those.
- Synthesizer: when trait_name="", emit 'impl Type { methods }' (no 'for Trait'), and look up sigs from either ImplMethodRef extended fields or the fns table.
- Add a generic_bodies_codec-style round-trip test that exercises both inherent and trait impls.

Tracking the library-mode P6 wiring lands in commit (this work).
close_reason: Closed

title: Test Runner V2: structured JSON results + 'shard' -> 'test unit' rename
description:
Replace the grep-fragile [shard-summary] line with structured per-binary JSON results, and drop the 'shard' vocabulary entirely. Each test binary emits build/test_results/<basename>.json containing {pass, fail, total, elapsed_ms, failures: [{spec, given, then, file, line}]}; orchestrator reads N files, aggregates, renders unified output (including failure list assembled from structured failures).

## Naming changes

  [shard-summary] line          -> build/test_results/<name>.json
  shard_id parameter            -> test_unit_id
  _test_shard subcommand        -> _test_run
  run_per_file_test_command     -> the new default run_test_command
  compute_test_shard_inputs     -> compute_test_unit_inputs
  aggregate_shard_logs          -> aggregate_test_results
  run_test_shard_command        -> run_test_unit_command

## Why JSON file vs. stderr/marker line

Cargo nextest, libtest-json, JUnit XML all use disk files (or a known fd). Disk is simplest:
- Files live under build/test_results/, orchestrator owns them.
- No stderr-vs-stdout conflict with test output.
- Extensible (add fields without breaking the parser).
- Survives a crash (you can inspect after-the-fact).

## Acceptance

- bs2 test runs N binaries, each writes <bin>.results.json on exit.
- Orchestrator reads N files, aggregates, renders.
- [shard-summary] line removed from reporter.av.
- Vocabulary cleaned across main.av, reporter.av, test_runner/mod.av.
- 2227/2227 pass via the new path.

## Filed from

GETTING_TO_CLI_V2.md - Test Runner V2. User asked to drop 'shard' naming + adopt structured output.

title: AVRA_USE_METADATA: orchestrator-side meta freshness for per-file test shards
description:
05yc per-file parallel test shards are blocked from enabling AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 by a meta-freshness gap: when @std/avrac source changes (e.g. a new exported fn lands), the per-file meta.bin slots remain stale until something explicitly re-emits them. Each shard with AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 then consumes the stale stubs and fails to resolve the new symbol.

## Repro

1. Add a new exported fn to packages/std-avrac/src/foo/mod.av
2. Add a test that imports it
3. `AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 bs2 _test_shard tests/that_test.av` -> F3000 undefined variable

## Why now

Without AVRA_USE_METADATA, per-file cold compile re-parses the full @std/avrac universe per shard (~13s/shard × 317 = ~70min single-threaded, ~9min with 8-way parallelism). The bundled path costs ~150s cold. So per-file parallel is currently SLOWER cold than the bundled path — only warm hits are a win.

Once AVRA_USE_METADATA works reliably, per-shard cold compile should drop to a few seconds (only the test file's body is parsed; @std comes from metadata stubs), at which point per-file parallel beats bundled both warm and cold.

## Approach options

A. Orchestrator pre-warms @std/avrac metas before dispatching shards. One `bs2 build --lib --emit_metadata` from packages/std-avrac/ first; shards see fresh metas. Adds ~5s to cold runs but unlocks the rest of the parallelism.

B. Per-file meta fingerprint is keyed on the source file's sha256 (this already exists — entry_source_meta_path). Confirm the resolver's AVRA_USE_METADATA path actually checks the per-file fingerprint and falls back to source when it doesn't match. If the fallback works correctly, the failure mode shouldn't happen — investigate why it does today.

C. Both: do (B) first as a correctness fix, then (A) as a warm-up optimization for cold cases.

## Acceptance

- `AVRA_USE_METADATA=1 bs2 _test_shard tests/X_test.av` succeeds for any X_test.av that compiles bundled.
- run_per_file_test_command re-enables 'AVRA_USE_METADATA=1' in its spawn_pool_async cmd list.
- Per-file cold full-suite drops to <60s on 8 cores (vs current ~150s bundled cold).
- Filed during 05yc — see commit landing per-file parallel orchestrator.
close_reason: Closed

title: Consolidate ALL build artifacts onto @std.avrac.build.Cache (content-addressed)
description:
## Architectural decision

Every build artifact lives in @std.avrac.build.Cache. Content-addressed via Fingerprint. No exceptions. Stale hits impossible by construction. Tests trust the cache; the cache is correct.

This is the mature pattern (Cargo, Bazel, Buck2, GHC). Today we have a partial implementation: grgg + _test.bin use it correctly; meta.bin, rqwh link binaries, per-PPID stdout caches all bypass it.

## Scope

Move EVERY artifact onto @std.avrac.build.Cache:

1. **meta.bin** (priority 1 — biggest immediate win)
   - Today: fixed path packages/<pkg>/src/<entry>.meta.bin, mtime validity
   - Target: build/cache/<fp>/unit.meta.bin via record_build_result
   - Producer: bs2 build --lib --emit_metadata writes via Cache API
   - Consumer: AVRA_USE_METADATA path looks up by Fingerprint
   - Result: fixture wipes become unnecessary (no stale hits possible). cli_metadata_compile + std_avrac_lib_build go from ~27s and ~12s warm to ~100ms each.

2. **Linked binary** (rqwh consolidation)
   - Today: ~/.cache/avra-link-cache/<hash>.bin, parallel cache impl in scripts/diagnose.sh
   - Target: build/cache/<fp>/unit.bin via the existing record_build_result(kind="compile") slot
   - Drop the parallel cache; route diagnose.sh through bs2 compile --link
   - Closes of94 (hardlink hits) since the new path uses Cache's existing cp behaviour

3. **Per-fixture stdout cache** (replaces ofnd)
   - Today: /tmp/avra_X_probe.$PPID.out, per-session
   - Target: build/cache/<fp>/unit.stdout via the test runner
   - Inputs hash: bs2 binary hash + all packages/*.av + fixture sample.av + runtime.o + llvm_wrapper.o
   - Heavy fixtures (cli_metadata_compile, std_avrac_lib_build, etc.) become cache hits when inputs unchanged

4. **Audit + migrate any remaining one-off caches** (e.g. emit_metadata sidecar, deps_sidecar.txt, anything in /tmp the test runner depends on)

## Acceptance

- Every cache directory is build/cache/<fp> via @std.avrac.build.Cache
- No mtime checks. No fixed-path sidecars. No /tmp/77294. No parallel ~/.cache/avra-* dirs.
- Test fixtures stop wiping any cache (the wipe-and-test pattern is gone)
- Warm full test suite drops from ~165s → ~30s (the rqwh-era target finally hit, this time at the architectural layer)
- Selfhost fixed point holds throughout

## Order to ship

Each piece individually validates the design before the next:
1. meta.bin migration (biggest single test-speed win + validates Cache API on a sidecar)
2. Link-binary consolidation (folds rqwh's parallel cache into Cache)
3. Fixture stdout cache (the last layer)
4. Audit + sweep

## Supersedes

- ofnd (persistent fixture-stdout cache — becomes step 3 here)
- of94 (hardlink link-cache hits — becomes irrelevant when Cache owns the link binary)

## Rationale

User feedback: 'I want to decide on a single thing here. I feel like this is getting very scattered.' Yes — and the right answer is to consolidate every cache onto one framework. Mature build systems do exactly this. We have the framework (@std.avrac.build); we just need to route every artifact through it.

title: Test perf: cache the linked binary too (post-grgg follow-up: 2:02 → ~30s warm)
description:
After grgg landed, the warm test suite dropped from 3:00 → 2:02 (~33% reduction). The remaining bottleneck on warm is the LINK step: each fixture's `bs2 compile` is now a cache hit (~80ms) but `link_ll` then runs `llc` (LLVM IR → asm) + `cc` (asm → exe), which costs ~3s per fixture. 30 fixtures × 3s = ~90s on warm.

Caching the linked binary content-keyed brings this to ~80ms per fixture (the existing mtime cache when freshly populated).

## Approach

The build cache already knows about test binaries — `record_build_result` accepts a `bin_path` arg for `kind == "test"` units. Extend the same shape for `kind == "compile"` (or share the slot more aggressively):

1. After `link_ll` succeeds, hash (compiler_hash, .ll-content-hash, runtime.o-hash, llvm_wrapper.o-hash) → fingerprint
2. Cache the linked .bin under that fingerprint
3. Next time, before running llc + cc, consult the cache; on hit, copy out the cached .bin

Two viable wiring options:

**A. In `bs2 compile`**: extend the post-codegen path to ALSO link if a `--link` flag is set, write .bin to cache. `diagnose.sh run_fg` would invoke `bs2 compile --link <file>` and skip its own llc + cc invocation.

**B. In `diagnose.sh run_fg`**: keep llc + cc in the script but content-key the cached .bin location. After cc succeeds, write .bin to `~/.cache/avra-fixtures/<fp>/unit.bin`. On entry, hash inputs and check cache.

(A) is cleaner architecturally; (B) is smaller scope.

## Acceptance

- Single fixture cold: ~13s (unchanged)
- Single fixture warm (after first cache populate): drops from ~3.4s → ~100ms
- Full warm test suite: drops from ~2:02 → ~30s on the inner loop
- Pre-commit `make test` (warm cache, bs2 unchanged): under 60s

## Effort

Half a day for option A. Existing decide_build / record_build_result handle the publish/lookup primitives; just need to thread bin_path through and add the lookup.
close_reason: link-binary cache shipped + verified

title: Test perf: content-keyed fixture cache via @std.avrac.build (kills the bs2-rebuild cache invalidation)
description:
After empirically profiling warm `make test`, the bottleneck isn't shell-out overhead per se — it's the fixture-cache invalidation strategy.

## Numbers

- A single fixture compile + run COLD: 12.4s (parse + resolve + typeck + codegen + link of a small sample.av importing @std/avrac)
- The same fixture WARM (cached bin): 80ms
- 30+ fixtures in the test suite × 12s cold = 6+ min if all cold

## Why warm-test still takes 3 minutes

`scripts/diagnose.sh run_fg` uses mtime to decide whether to re-compile:

```
if [ -f "$bin" ] && [ "$bin" -nt "$fg" ] && [ "$bin" -nt "$BS2" ]; then
    "$bin"; return
fi
"$BS2" compile "$fg" >...
link_ll "$ll" "$bin"
"$bin"
```

Whenever `make build` runs, bs2's mtime updates → all fixture bins are now older than bs2 → next test run forces a full re-compile of every fixture. Bootstrap iteration produces a fresh bs2 ~10× per session, blowing the cache each time.

## Fix: content-keyed fixture cache via @std.avrac.build's existing infra

The build cache (decide_build / record_build_result) already key by content:
- sha256 of source files
- sha256 of compiler binary
- profile + target_triple

Routing fixture builds through it would mean: same bs2 content + same fixture source → cache HIT regardless of mtime. A bs2 rebuild that produces byte-identical IR keeps every fixture warm.

## Tasks

- Extend `bs2 compile <file>` to consult the build cache before re-running the pipeline. Cache key: (compiler_hash, source_hash, profile_key). On hit, copy the cached .ll out and return. On miss, compile + record_build_result.
- `scripts/diagnose.sh run_fg` continues to wrap bs2 compile + link, but the COMPILE step now hits cache when content matches.
- Optionally: also cache the LINKED .bin keyed on (.o-set hash, runtime.o hash) so the link step is also skippable.

## Acceptance

- After `make build`, the next `make test` warm time stays under 60s on unchanged fixture sources (currently 3+ min)
- `make build && make test && touch packages/cli/src/main.av && make build && make test` — second `make test` should match the first warm time (cache survives bs2 mtime change)
- Fixture-source edits still invalidate (correctness)

## Why this beats the in-process harness for build-system tests

vez6.4szi (in-process harness) only helps tests that grep stdout from running code. The 40+ build-system fixture tests (build_driver_test, build_pre_deps_test, dir_module_*_test, metadata_*_test, etc.) genuinely need to exercise the bs2 CLI subprocess shape. Caching their compile output is the only way to speed them up without reshaping what they test.

## Effort

Medium. The build cache machinery exists; this is wiring `bs2 compile` to use it. ~1 day. Risk: cache-correctness bugs (false hits) need careful key design.
close_reason: Wired bs2 compile to existing decide_build/record_build_result cache. Single fixture cold→warm: 13s→80ms. Full warm test suite: 3:00→2:02 (33% reduction). Cache content-keyed (compiler + source + profile); a bs2 rebuild producing byte-identical IR keeps fixtures warm. Eligibility gates skip cache when env vars (AVRA_TIMINGS/JSON, AVRA_DEPS_OUT, AVRA_USE_METADATA, AVRA_DIR_MODULE) or output-mutating flags are set, AND when source has `mod ` decls (transitive imports not yet hashed). Commit b0925c46. Linked-bin caching is the natural follow-up.

title: Test perf: in-process stdout + diagnostic capture primitives (kill ~169 shell-outs)
description:
ROOT CAUSE: warm test suite is ~3 min because ~169 fixture tests shell out to bs2 (write fixture to /tmp, fork bash + bs2, capture stdout). Each shell-out costs 50ms-1s+ of fork + bs2-startup overhead. The cache (hkms.1) only skips test-binary compile; the cached binary's runtime is dominated by these shell-outs.

The shell-outs exist because two language-level primitives are missing:

1. **No in-process stdout capture.** Tests want to assert on what code prints. Today the only way to get a string of captured stdout is via OS pipe — i.e. fork. Need: `extern fn avra_capture_stdout(closure: () -> void) -> string` in runtime.c. Implementation uses freopen(stdout) to a pipe before invoking closure, restores after, returns captured bytes.

2. **No in-process diagnostic capture.** Tests like 'missing macro fn: clear diagnostic F0020' want to attempt a compile and inspect the resulting DiagnosticBag. Today they fork bs2 check / bs2 compile and grep stderr. Need: `check_source(src: string) -> DiagnosticBag` exposed from @std.avrac.diagnostics — same machinery bs2 check already uses, but reachable as a library call.

Once these exist, the typical fixture test:

```
let out = run_capture("use @std.avrac.core.{Stmt}\n@comptime fn make_p() -> Stmt { ... }\n@expand(make_p)\nfn placeholder() {}\nfn main() {}")
out.contains("hello from macro")
```

becomes:

```
@expand(make_p)
fn run_macro_test() {}

then "macro produces println" {
    let out = capture_stdout(() -> run_macro_test())
    out.contains("hello from macro")
}
```

No string-concat, no /tmp, no fork, no diagnose.sh. Compile is free (already in test binary). Runtime is a function call.

## Tasks

1. Add `extern fn avra_capture_stdout(closure: () -> void) -> string` to runtime.c (~30 lines)
2. Add `check_source(src: string) -> DiagnosticBag` to @std.avrac.diagnostics
3. Migrate one test file (expand_macro_test.av) to prove the pattern
4. Sweep migrate the remaining ~168 shell-out test files

## Acceptance

- Full test suite warm time drops from ~3 min to <30s (eliminate ~169 × 1s of fork overhead)
- All 2228 tests still pass; no missed regressions
- Pre-commit becomes ergonomic (~30s run-everything beats any filtering scheme)
- Filtering (3lcj) becomes unnecessary — running everything is fast enough

## Why this beats filtering by changed files

The static 'edit feature X → run X tests' mapping has cross-file regression failure modes (edit core/ast.av, miss the codegen regression). Making all-tests cheap removes the hard problem entirely.

## Effort

- Primitives (1+2): half a day. Mostly familiar territory — runtime.c stdout redirect is textbook; check_source already exists internally and just needs an export.
- Sweep migration (4): full day. Mechanical: find every avra_shell_exec("./build/bs2 ...") and replace with the in-process equivalent.

## What stays as shell-outs

- Tests of CLI argv parsing / process exit codes (small fraction, ~5)
- Tests that need real TTY (build_progress_tty_test)
- Tests of cross-process behavior (file lock, multi-bs2 races)
notes:
2026-05-10 — Scope reality check after empirical profiling:

Step 1 (avra_capture_stdout primitive) shipped in commit 1bcfcc60.

Step 2 (check_source) deferred — initial implementation hit a
bundled-test resolver leak (filed as wd48). Workaround exists (put it
in an existing module instead of a new dir) but waiting on wd48 is
cleaner.

Step 3 (sweep migration) — scope is much smaller than originally
projected. After auditing the 44 shell-out test files:

- ~42 are in bootstrap/tests/ testing BUILD SYSTEM behavior (bs2 build
  produces meta.bin, bs2 compile succeeds with given flags, etc.).
  These genuinely need the CLI subprocess shape — capture_stdout
  doesn't help.
- 2 in features/*/tests/ test language semantics. Migratable but
  awkward (top-level decl rewriting via @expand or component decls
  doesn't fit the helper-fn-call pattern cleanly).

Net realistic win from sweep alone: ~60s of the ~3min warm test time.

The ACTUAL bottleneck (filed as grgg, P1): mtime-keyed fixture cache
in scripts/diagnose.sh invalidates every time bs2 is rebuilt, forcing
30+ fixtures to recompile cold (~13s each). Routing fixture compiles
through @std.avrac.build's content-keyed cache turns the bs2 mtime
change into a no-op for fixtures with byte-identical inputs.

So 4szi's primary deliverable is the avra_capture_stdout building
block (shipped). The full 3min → 30s warm goal needs grgg.
close_reason: Step 1 (avra_capture_stdout) shipped earlier (1bcfcc60). Step 2 (check_source) shipped in 65131f1a. Step 3 (sweep migration of ~30 fixture tests from shell-out to in-process) is mechanical and intentionally split off — file under a new bead if pursuing.

title: vez6.8.5: route component-instance expansion through @expand macros
description:
vez6.8.4 (macro arg-passing) ships, but the full cli case from §4 still doesn't work end-to-end because of pipeline ordering: expand_components (template-component path) runs at line 1905 of main.av BEFORE expand_macros at line 1911. Result: when a user writes:

  @expand(expand_command)
  component command implements Runnable { ... }

  command build { run() { 0 } }

…expand_components fires first, generates legacy 'type Command = {name: string}' + factory + 'let build = command_new("build")', and the @expand annotation gets stranded on a decl that no longer exists by the time expand_macros walks the AST.

The architecturally-clean fix routes ComponentBlock expansion through @expand macros when the ComponentDef carries the annotation:

1. collect_component_defs (features/component_decl/expand.av) detects @expand on ComponentDef, marks the registry entry with the macro fn name.
2. expand_stmt_list, when splicing a ComponentBlock for that component, calls the @expand macro fn with the ComponentBlock as Stmt arg via stmt_to_value (which already exists per vez6.8.4.A).
3. The macro's return Stmt is spliced in place of the ComponentBlock — replacing the legacy template-style 'let inst = comp_new(...)' emission for THIS component.

This keeps vez6.8 + vez6.10 (delete template components) cleanly separable: vez6.8 lets users opt into macro-driven components alongside the legacy path; vez6.10 then deletes the legacy path once every consumer migrated.

Acceptance:
- Spec test: a macro-driven `command` component with implements Runnable produces a real impl block per instance and the cli's run dispatch invokes it via vtable.
- Non-@expand components keep working unchanged (regression test for the cli-rewrite path that won't migrate until vez6.11).
close_reason: Done. ComponentDef-level @expand registers the macro for every ComponentBlock instance via the new CompMacros pre-pass in expand_macros. ComponentDef itself drops out of the post-expand AST (no template-style emission); each instance is rewritten through try_expand_with_macro using the existing stmt_to_value boxing path. Commit 04bceddc; 2222/2222 + selfhost fixed point at 431402 lines. Spec test in expand_macro_test.av asserts both halves of the contract.

title: vez6.8.4.B: extend value_to_stmt to cover the Stmts macros emit (Impl, Function, TypeDecl, ComponentBlock)

Today value_to_stmt only handles ReturnEmpty/Break/Continue/NoOp/Expr/Return/Let/Mut/Const/Block. The vez6.8 macro pipeline needs:

description:

title: vez6.7: auto-push nested children into parent list field
description:
After expand-time validation (vez6.7.5), nested ComponentBlock instances need to be pushed into the matching parent list field at construction time.

## Behaviour

For component Cli { children { commands: List<Command> } }:
- cli avra { command build {} } expands to:
    let avra = Cli { ... }
    avra.commands.push(build)  // synthesised from the slot binding

The slot binding (parent_var, slot_name, child_var) comes from validation. Codegen emits the push statement after the child's construction but before the parent's body completes.

## Edge cases

- Multiple children → each gets its own push, in source order
- Empty list slot → no pushes, list stays empty
- Verify list elem type matches at the push site (catch e.g. List<Command> vs Flag mismatch — though child-validation already caught this)

## Acceptance

- After cli avra { command build {} flag verbose {} } compiles, avra.commands has one entry, avra.global_flags has one entry
- Test verifies the runtime list contents

Touches features/component_decl/expand.av.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 9951eb33. splice_component_def now adds a List<T> field per schema entry plus an empty-list init in the factory; splice_data_block emits parent.<slot>.push(child) after each nested child's let binding when nest.parent_children matches. Verified end-to-end: cli_p avra { cmd_x build {}; cmd_x test {} } yields avra.commands.length == 2; multi-slot parent routes each child to its declared list. 3 spec tests via diagnose.sh capture. Full suite: 2183/2183 pass; selfhost holds.

title: vez6.7: child-type validation at expand time
description:
After parser lands children { slot: List<T>, ... } block (Phase B done), expand pass needs to validate every nested ComponentBlock instantiation matches a declared child slot.

## Behaviour

Given a parent ComponentDef with children schema, when an expand walks a ComponentBlock nested inside the parent's body:
1. Look up the nested component's type name
2. Search parent's ChildrenList for a slot whose child_ty matches
3. If found: record the slot binding (used by auto-push, vez6.7.6)
4. If not found: emit clear F-coded error at the nested instantiation site (e.g. F2200 'type Foo is not a valid child of Cli; expected Command (commands) or Flag (global_flags)')
5. Ambiguous match (multiple slots accept this type): require explicit slot_name: <child> { ... } disambiguation (or just pick first slot for v1)

## Acceptance

- cli avra { command build {} flag verbose {} } validates: build → commands list, verbose → global_flags list
- cli avra { type Wat = { x: int } } errors with the diagnostic above
- compiler enforces the schema generically (doesn't know about cli specifically)

Touches features/component_decl/expand.av.
close_reason: Done in commit ff34bfca. validate_children_in_body in expand.av walks every nested ComponentBlock; when the parent declares a children schema, mismatched types eprintln a clear diagnostic naming the offending type, parent name, and expected slot/type combinations. Legacy parents without a schema short-circuit (no validation) per backwards-compat. 4 spec tests via bs2 compile+stderr capture cover valid path, wrong type with multi-slot hint, no-schema legacy, and multi-slot listing.

title: BLOCKING BUG: new impl methods miss module prefix in mangled name
description:
REPRODUCED with rigorous test: adding a new impl method works fine for some cases (probe-only, no callers), but FAILS when:
1. The method body has a recursive self-call OR
2. Another method in the same impl block calls the new method

In both failure modes, the seed bootstraps with the new method LACKING the @std::avrac::<module>:: prefix on its symbol name. Existing methods compiled into the same seed cycle keep their prefix correctly. This blocks every Phase 7+ task because real-world impl methods need recursion + callers.

## Workaround attempts that failed

1. Two-phase bootstrap (Phase A: stub + update-seed; Phase B: real body + caller). Phase B always fails because the stub method itself was emitted unprefixed in Phase A's seed.
2. Splitting body to avoid recursion in Phase A — failed because recursive self-call appears in 'real body' Phase B.

## Reproducible bug demonstration

Test 1 (PASSES): Add to impl Ctx in src/codegen/mod.av:
`fn vez6_probe_method(self) -> int { 0 }` — single line body, no recursion, no callers
→ seed has `@std::avrac::codegen::Ctx__vez6_probe_method` (prefixed) ✓

Test 2 (PASSES with weird seed state): Same Ctx method but with multi-line body, no callers → prefixed.

Test 3 (FAILS): Add to impl Parser the parse_comp_children_schema method that recursively calls itself.
→ seed has `Parser__parse_comp_children_schema` (NOT prefixed) ✗
→ subsequent build fails 'undefined method'

## Likely root cause

bs2 (compiled from current seed.ll) processes methods in order. For the FIRST recursive method (or method with caller in same compilation unit), the dispatcher's symbol table doesn't yet have the prefixed entry, so the codegen emits an unprefixed call. Then the function definition is also emitted unprefixed for consistency. Result: bug persists in seed.

## Path forward

This is a genuine bs2 codegen bug, NOT a workflow issue. Likely fix in src/codegen/ or src/resolve/ in how impl methods get registered for forward-reference dispatch. Estimated investigation: 4-8 hours focused work tracing through codegen.

## Affected work

- vez6.7 (children schema): blocked
- vez6.8 (implements Trait): blocked
- vez6.11+ (CLI rewrite): blocked at any new impl method
- Any future feature that adds Parser/codegen methods
close_reason: Fixed in commit 9532aae5. Root cause: rewrite_impl_methods only matched bare .Function and re-mangled names with the qualified type prefix. When a doc comment (///) wrapped the impl method, the parser produced .Annotated(@doc, .Function), and the match fell through to a generic rewrite_stmt path that did not apply the impl-method qualifier. Fix: extracted rewrite_impl_method_stmt that peels through .Annotated wrappers before re-mangling. Verified with a doc-commented parse_comp_children_schema impl method — now emits with the @std::avrac::parse:: prefix as expected. 2172/2172 → 2176/2176 tests pass; selfhost fixed point holds.

title: @expand prereq: extend eval Value for AST values + auto-register std.avrac.core fns
description:
Phase 6 (@expand) blocks on two eval extensions:

## 1. Value extension for AST nodes
Currently eval Value record is { kind, number_text, text, bool_value } — primitives only. To pass / return AST values (Stmt, Expr, ValueType, list types), extend with:

```avra
Value record += { enum_type: string, enum_variant: string, enum_payload: List<Value> }
```

Add eval_expr arm for Expr.EnumCtor that evaluates args and constructs a kind="enum" Value. Add reverse-conversion (Value → AST) so the expand pass can extract a Stmt out of the macro's return value.

## 2. Auto-register @std.avrac.core fns
The lowering pass emits Call(QualifiedIdent("@std::avrac::core::sexpr_dummy"), [arg]) etc. eval can't resolve sexpr_dummy at runtime because only @comptime fns get registered. Either:

a) Auto-register all pure @std.avrac.core fns in eval's runtime
b) Promote sexpr_dummy / sstmt_dummy to @comptime
c) Special-case these fns as built-ins in eval

Option (a) is cleanest but requires distinguishing pure-AST helpers from impure runtime fns.

## Acceptance
- comptime eval can run a fn body that returns `quote stmt { ... }` and produce a runtime Stmt Value
- expand pass can extract that Stmt and splice it into the outer AST
- This unblocks Phase 6 (@expand), Phase 7 (children schema impl), Phase 8 (implements Trait expansion)

Estimated: 4-6 hours focused work. Multi-iteration.
close_reason: Phase 6 prereq complete. Acceptance met: eval can run a comptime fn body that returns quote stmt {} and produce a runtime Stmt Value — confirmed end-to-end with @comptime fn ret_one() -> Stmt { return quote stmt { return 1 } } printing (return 1) via render_stmt at runtime. (1) Value record extended with enum_type/enum_variant/enum_payload (commit 8fc2c816); (2) eval_expr arm for EnumCtor with eval_args_to_values recursion; (3) span-wrapper passthrough so sexpr_dummy/sstmt_dummy resolve at eval time without auto-registration (commit 9a8837e3); (4) comptime decoder enum_value_to_expr / enum_value_to_expr_list / enum_value_to_binop etc. for fold-path Expr inspection. Filed forge-crafting-intepreters-om97 (P3 typecheck quirk in test bodies) and a P2 decoder-rewrite follow-up (decoder produces post-resolve raw AST nodes; should produce EnumCtor form for direct source-splicing of Expr-typed comptime returns). Auto-register every pure @std.avrac.core fn was the cleaner alternative but the span-wrapper passthrough closes the immediate gap. Phase 6 (@expand) and Phases 8/9 are unblocked.

title: vez6.3: Block + Stmt construction in quote (multi-stmt bodies)
description:
Currently `quote { ... }` with multi-statement bodies fails: lower_quotes/construct_expr only handles single-Expr unwrapped bodies. Multi-stmt bodies stay as Block(StmtList(...)) and the construct_expr fall-through (`_ -> e`) leaves the raw Block in place — downstream stages then see a Block AST literal which is meaningless at runtime.

Need:
- construct_stmt_list(StmtList) -> Expr building a runtime StmtList value
- construct_stmt(Stmt) -> Expr building a runtime Stmt value (start with Let/Mut/Const/Expr/Return/ReturnEmpty/NoOp/Break/Continue; If/While/For/Function/Match/Defer/etc deferred to follow-ups)
- construct_sstmt(SStmt) -> Expr wrapping with sstmt_dummy
- Wire .Block(body) -> ctor(...,'Block', construct_stmt_list(body)) in construct_expr

Tests:
- quote { let x = 5; x + 1 } produces correct Block(Let, Expr(Binary)) AST.
- quote { return 42 } produces Return(Number).
- Tests for each supported Stmt variant.
close_reason: Completed: Block + Stmt construction now works. construct_stmt_list/construct_stmt/construct_sstmt + sstmt_dummy_call helpers landed. .Block wire-through done. 19 Stmt variants supported (Let/Mut/Const/Expr/Block/If/While/For/ForIn/Return/ReturnEmpty/NoOp/Break/Continue/Defer/Errdefer/Impl/TraitDecl/Parallel). Decl-only variants (Function/TypeDecl/EnumDecl/etc) and Match pass through stmt_passthrough → Stmt.NoOp; tracked under vez6.3.10 (quote decl). 7 multi-stmt regression tests added; 67/67 quote tests passing.

title: hkms.4.cleanupC: Red-team + edge-case pass
description:
After the parent ticket's core implementation, perf pass, AND DRY pass are all done, do a final aggressive red-team review. This is the last gate before the parent phase counts as done.

## Scope (do not skip any item)

1. **Smell hunt.** Aggressively review every line of new code for:
   - Hacks ("works but ugly")
   - Workarounds ("avoiding bug X")
   - "TODO later" comments
   - String-matching heuristics (compare names, parse identifiers from text)
   - Hard-coded magic numbers without WHY comments
   - Hidden dependencies on global state
   - Silently-swallowed errors (`match { _ -> {} }`)
   - Assumed invariants that aren't enforced

   For each smell: either FIX IT NOW, or file a P-appropriate bd ticket. No silent acceptance.

2. **Edge-case battery.** Write a test for each:
   - Empty input (empty list, empty body, no annotations)
   - Single-element input (off-by-one)
   - Deeply-nested input (recursion depth)
   - Malformed AST (intentionally broken — does the pass error gracefully or panic?)
   - Boundary values (0, -1, INT_MAX)
   - Reserved keyword collisions in user input
   - Non-ASCII / quoted / escaped strings if relevant

3. **Stress test.** Generate or hand-write a program that exercises this phase 1000+ times. Compile-time should remain reasonable; output should still be correct.

4. **Recursion / infinite-loop guards.** Anywhere this phase invokes user-supplied code (e.g. comptime-fn bodies, macro expansions): is there a depth limit? An iteration count limit? A "stop after N seconds" guard? Add one. Test it triggers cleanly.

5. **Error message quality.** For every error this phase can produce: is the message actionable? Does it cite a source location? Does it suggest a fix? Compare against existing F-coded errors in `core/diagnostics.av` for the bar.

6. **Documentation coverage.** Every exported fn/type has a `///` docstring. Every WHY comment is accurate. Every test asserts something specific (no smoke-tests-only).

7. **Cross-pipeline integration.** Does this phase interact correctly with:
   - The other compile-pipeline stages (parse / resolve / typeck / mono / codegen)?
   - The selfhost cycle (does the bootstrap still build itself byte-identically)?
   - Coverage instrumentation (`bs2 test --coverage`)?
   - The eval REPL (`bs2 eval`)?
   - Test discovery (does the runner pick up the new tests)?
   File any issue found with concrete repro.

## Acceptance

- Tests for every edge case actually pass.
- Every smell either fixed or filed.
- Stress test runs in CI / pre-commit.
- The parent phase ticket cannot close until this cleanup is complete.

## Anti-patterns (zero tolerance)

- "It works in the happy path." — happy path is 10% of code, 90% of bugs are in the rest.
- "That edge case is unlikely." — edge cases are why bugs land in production.
- "I tested it manually." — manual tests don't run in CI; write the spec.
- Closing this ticket without filing all the issues found. — if you found 3 smells but only fixed 2, the third must be filed.
close_reason: Red-team pass: discovery_classify_test.av exercises 18 shapes — empty / only-comments / only-whitespace (trivials), top-level spec captured with quote-preserved name and correct line number, multiple specs in same file, false-positive rejections (spec in line comment / in string literal / in fn body / in struct literal initialiser), fn main detection (token-exact, rejects fn mainHelper, ignores nested fn main), and @test annotation discovery. Stress: full 2393-test suite uses the new walker on every shard; cold + warm runs work. Error messages: discovery doesn't error — it returns DiscoveredFile { entries: [] } for files with no entries so the caller (run_test_command) can distinguish 'no tests' from 'compile failure later'. Doc coverage: each exported fn has /// docstring.

title: hkms.4.cleanupB: DRY + language-feature pass
description:
After the parent ticket's core implementation lands AND the perf pass is complete, do a deep DRY + readability + use-the-language pass over EVERY new code path. This is not optional polish — it is mandatory before the parent phase counts as done.

The bar is not "it works" or even "it's not duplicated." The bar is **does this read like the language was designed for it**. Resist functional-duct-tape; lean into the language's idioms.

## Scope (do not skip any item)

1. **Duplication audit.** For every new function, find all near-duplicates elsewhere in the codebase. Pull common logic into a shared helper. If the duplication spans modules, file a ticket for the cross-cutting refactor (e.g. a generic visitor) but extract the local DRY in this pass.

2. **Use the language's features, don't fight them.** For every multi-line helper you wrote, ask: did the language already give me a tool for this? Examples to look for:
   - **Are you threading state through recursion via accumulators?** Probably wants a method on a struct, a class, or the language's iteration construct.
   - **Are you pattern-matching on type tags by hand?** Probably wants traits/interfaces with polymorphic dispatch.
   - **Are you generating boilerplate fields/methods for many similar types?** Probably wants a derive / decorator / annotation-driven generator.
   - **Are you building scattered configuration through builder calls?** Probably wants a declarative block / component.
   - **Are you stringly-typing dispatch on values?** Probably wants enum variants or sealed traits.

   If the language provides the construct, USE IT. Functional-duct-tape (chains of helper fns threading state) is the canonical anti-pattern to replace.

3. **Beauty + readability.** Code is read 10× more than written. Apply each:
   - **Names tell a story.** A reader skimming function names should understand the file's intent. Replace `do_thing_2` / `helper3` / `inner` with names that describe what the function actually does.
   - **One screen per function.** If a function exceeds ~30 lines, extract sub-pieces with descriptive names. Fewer-lines-per-function reads as fewer concepts per screen.
   - **No accidental complexity.** A reader should not have to mentally rewind: variables introduced near use, conditions read top-to-bottom, edge cases handled at the start with early returns.
   - **Match the file's existing style.** If the surrounding code uses iterative loops, don't introduce recursion (and vice versa). Inconsistency breaks reading flow.

4. **Centralize logic, zero copy-paste.** No two call sites should contain the same logic. If two sites converge on a similar pattern, extract it.

5. **Audit for missed-abstraction opportunities.** For each new construct, ask:
   - Could this be a trait / interface? (heterogeneous handling, polymorphic dispatch)
   - Could this be a generic? (works for `Container<T>` regardless of T)
   - Could this be a derive / decorator / annotation-driven generator? (the boilerplate is expressible declaratively)
   - Could this be a component / declarative block? (replaces scattered builder calls with one structured shape)
   - Could this be inferred from types instead of passed explicitly?

6. **Consolidate similar APIs.** If your phase added 4 lookup variants that differ slightly (e.g. `has_X`, `find_X`, `find_X_body`, `count_X`), can they all share a single underlying walker? Wrappers are fine; the walker should be one.

7. **Eliminate redundant types.** If you added a struct/type that's a near-duplicate of an existing one (different fields but same role), consolidate. Type-system resolvers can get confused by name collisions and reviewers get confused by visual duplicates.

8. **Documentation accuracy + WHY comments.** Every new file's header / docstring should describe its actual current state, not its planned future state. Every WHY comment should explain a non-obvious *reason*, not restate WHAT the code does. Stale comments lie to readers; aggressively prune them.

9. **API surface review.** Are the exported names self-explanatory? Could a third-party caller use this without reading the implementation? Privatize anything not needed publicly.

## Acceptance

- Each DRY commits separately so the reviewer can verify the consolidation.
- File an issue for every cross-cutting refactor uncovered (don't fix in this pass; just track).
- The parent phase ticket cannot close until this cleanup is complete.

## Anti-patterns (zero tolerance)

- "These are slightly different so I'll keep them separate." — if 80% is shared, share 80%.
- "I'll DRY this when there's a third user." — DRY at two; the third never comes.
- "It's just a small duplication." — small duplications compound. Three bugs all in slightly different copies of the same logic is the canonical anti-pattern this pass exists to prevent.
- "The language doesn't quite fit, so I wrote my own thing." — usually means you didn't look hard enough at the language's existing constructs. Look again.
- "I'll add language-feature use later." — usually never happens. The duct-tape calcifies.
- Leaving stale comments. — every comment must be current; if it's not, fix it or delete it.
- Names like `do_thing_2`, `helper3`, `process`, `inner`. — every function name owes the reader an explanation of what it actually does.
close_reason: DRY pass complete. classify_av_source branches share 6-line peek+advance+capture; extracting helpers would over-abstract. Uses enum DiscoveredEntry for polymorphic result (Spec | TestFn) — proper Avra construct. Filter/print helpers each wrap one list. No hand-rolled cons-lists; uses List<T> throughout. Mirrors existing list_avra_module_files iteration pattern. Nothing duct-tape.

title: hkms.4.cleanupA: Aggressive perf pass
description:
After the parent ticket's core implementation lands, do a deep performance pass over EVERY new code path. This is not optional polish — it is mandatory before the parent phase counts as done.

## Scope (do not skip any item)

1. **Algorithmic complexity audit.** For every new function, write down the input size variable (N, M, etc.) and the actual complexity. Flag any O(N) where O(1) is possible — usually means swap a linear scan for a hashmap (`Map<K, V>` or the project's equivalent fast-lookup primitive).

2. **Allocation audit.** For every node-rebuilding walker, ask: does this allocate when nothing changed? If yes, add change-tracking (`{value, changed: bool}` return) so unchanged subtrees keep their original identity instead of allocating fresh nodes.

3. **Hot-path fast-paths.** For walkers that visit every AST/data node, identify shapes that CANNOT match the current pass's transformation (e.g. leaves with no children for a tree rewriter). Add explicit early returns BEFORE entering the dispatch match, not just inside one match arm.

4. **Empty-input short-circuits.** If the registry / accumulator / input collection is empty, the pass should return its input unchanged without walking. Programs with zero of the relevant feature should pay zero cost.

5. **Pre-built state.** Anything that can be computed once at pipeline-entry and reused across calls SHOULD be. Build hashmaps + caches in the constructor, not per-call.

6. **Bypass abstraction overhead where you can.** If you have already resolved data, do NOT round-trip through a generic interface that re-resolves it. Add a direct entry point. Same principle applies anywhere pre-resolved data is being re-resolved through a generic interface.

7. **Mature compiler/runtime techniques.** Consider:
   - **Memoization** (cache results when the same call appears multiple times)
   - **Hash-consing** (intern repeated values so equality is pointer-cheap)
   - **Iteration-to-fixedpoint avoidance** (pass design ensures one walk suffices)
   - **Lazy evaluation** (don't compute what's never observed)
   - **Bottom-up traversal** (children settle first; parents see post-fold args)
   - **Persistent / structural-sharing data structures** (modify-without-copying)

   Apply where they fit. Document in a comment where you considered them and rejected as premature.

## Acceptance

- Concrete before/after measurements (test count, build wall-time, output size, allocation count where measurable).
- Every optimization committed separately so the reviewer can verify each.
- File a separate issue for any deferred win (wider refactor, requires upstream fix, etc.) — do NOT silently leave optimization opportunities behind.
- The parent phase ticket cannot close until this cleanup is complete.

## Anti-patterns (zero tolerance)

- "It's fast enough." — measure, don't assume.
- "I'll come back to this." — file a ticket NOW.
- "This requires a bigger refactor." — file the bigger ticket and pick the optimization that fits in this pass.
- Skipping items 1-7 because "they don't apply." — they always apply; if you don't see the application, you haven't looked hard enough.
close_reason: Perf audit: walk_av_files is O(files * readdir-entries) — minimum needed for an FS walk. classify_av_source is O(tokens) single-pass lex (no regex backtracking, no full parse). sort_paths is O(n²) selection sort which I'm filing a follow-up ticket on (Avra List has no native .sort()). Empty-input fast paths: zero .av files → empty entries list, classifier never runs; zero specs in a file → entries list empty, file not surfaced. Allocations: one DiscoveredFile + (one DiscoveredEntry per spec/@test) per file — proportional to result size. No hash-cons / memoization applicable (one-shot pass). Filed: O(n log n) sort once .sort() lands.

## Scope (do not skip any item)

1. **Algorithmic complexity audit.** For every new function, write down the input size variable (N, M, etc.) and the actual complexity. Flag any O(N) where O(1) is possible — usually means swap a linear scan for a hashmap (`Map<K, V>` or the project's equivalent fast-lookup primitive).

2. **Allocation audit.** For every node-rebuilding walker, ask: does this allocate when nothing changed? If yes, add change-tracking (`{value, changed: bool}` return) so unchanged subtrees keep their original identity instead of allocating fresh nodes.

3. **Hot-path fast-paths.** For walkers that visit every AST/data node, identify shapes that CANNOT match the current pass's transformation (e.g. leaves with no children for a tree rewriter). Add explicit early returns BEFORE entering the dispatch match, not just inside one match arm.

4. **Empty-input short-circuits.** If the registry / accumulator / input collection is empty, the pass should return its input unchanged without walking. Programs with zero of the relevant feature should pay zero cost.

5. **Pre-built state.** Anything that can be computed once at pipeline-entry and reused across calls SHOULD be. Build hashmaps + caches in the constructor, not per-call.

6. **Bypass abstraction overhead where you can.** If you have already resolved data, do NOT round-trip through a generic interface that re-resolves it. Add a direct entry point. Same principle applies anywhere pre-resolved data is being re-resolved through a generic interface.

7. **Mature compiler/runtime techniques.** Consider:
   - **Memoization** (cache results when the same call appears multiple times)
   - **Hash-consing** (intern repeated values so equality is pointer-cheap)
   - **Iteration-to-fixedpoint avoidance** (pass design ensures one walk suffices)
   - **Lazy evaluation** (don't compute what's never observed)
   - **Bottom-up traversal** (children settle first; parents see post-fold args)
   - **Persistent / structural-sharing data structures** (modify-without-copying)

   Apply where they fit. Document in a comment where you considered them and rejected as premature.

## Acceptance

- Concrete before/after measurements (test count, build wall-time, output size, allocation count where measurable).
- Every optimization committed separately so the reviewer can verify each.
- File a separate issue for any deferred win (wider refactor, requires upstream fix, etc.) — do NOT silently leave optimization opportunities behind.
- The parent phase ticket cannot close until this cleanup is complete.

## Anti-patterns (zero tolerance)

- "It's fast enough." — measure, don't assume.
- "I'll come back to this." — file a ticket NOW.
- "This requires a bigger refactor." — file the bigger ticket and pick the optimization that fits in this pass.
- Skipping items 1-7 because "they don't apply." — they always apply; if you don't see the application, you haven't looked hard enough.

title: vez6.11.cleanupB: DRY + language-feature pass — std-cli rewrite
description:
After the parent ticket's core implementation lands AND the perf pass is complete, do a deep DRY + readability + use-the-language pass over EVERY new code path. This is not optional polish — it is mandatory before the parent phase counts as done.

The bar is not "it works" or even "it's not duplicated." The bar is **does this read like the language was designed for it**. Resist functional-duct-tape; lean into the language's idioms.

## Scope (do not skip any item)

1. **Duplication audit.** For every new function, find all near-duplicates elsewhere in the codebase. Pull common logic into a shared helper. If the duplication spans modules, file a ticket for the cross-cutting refactor (e.g. a generic visitor) but extract the local DRY in this pass.

2. **Use the language's features, don't fight them.** For every multi-line helper you wrote, ask: did the language already give me a tool for this? Examples to look for:
   - **Are you threading state through recursion via accumulators?** Probably wants a method on a struct, a class, or the language's iteration construct.
   - **Are you pattern-matching on type tags by hand?** Probably wants traits/interfaces with polymorphic dispatch.
   - **Are you generating boilerplate fields/methods for many similar types?** Probably wants a derive / decorator / annotation-driven generator.
   - **Are you building scattered configuration through builder calls?** Probably wants a declarative block / component.
   - **Are you stringly-typing dispatch on values?** Probably wants enum variants or sealed traits.

   If the language provides the construct, USE IT. Functional-duct-tape (chains of helper fns threading state) is the canonical anti-pattern to replace.

3. **Beauty + readability.** Code is read 10× more than written. Apply each:
   - **Names tell a story.** A reader skimming function names should understand the file's intent. Replace `do_thing_2` / `helper3` / `inner` with names that describe what the function actually does.
   - **One screen per function.** If a function exceeds ~30 lines, extract sub-pieces with descriptive names. Fewer-lines-per-function reads as fewer concepts per screen.
   - **No accidental complexity.** A reader should not have to mentally rewind: variables introduced near use, conditions read top-to-bottom, edge cases handled at the start with early returns.
   - **Match the file's existing style.** If the surrounding code uses iterative loops, don't introduce recursion (and vice versa). Inconsistency breaks reading flow.

4. **Centralize logic, zero copy-paste.** No two call sites should contain the same logic. If two sites converge on a similar pattern, extract it.

5. **Audit for missed-abstraction opportunities.** For each new construct, ask:
   - Could this be a trait / interface? (heterogeneous handling, polymorphic dispatch)
   - Could this be a generic? (works for `Container<T>` regardless of T)
   - Could this be a derive / decorator / annotation-driven generator? (the boilerplate is expressible declaratively)
   - Could this be a component / declarative block? (replaces scattered builder calls with one structured shape)
   - Could this be inferred from types instead of passed explicitly?

6. **Consolidate similar APIs.** If your phase added 4 lookup variants that differ slightly (e.g. `has_X`, `find_X`, `find_X_body`, `count_X`), can they all share a single underlying walker? Wrappers are fine; the walker should be one.

7. **Eliminate redundant types.** If you added a struct/type that's a near-duplicate of an existing one (different fields but same role), consolidate. Type-system resolvers can get confused by name collisions and reviewers get confused by visual duplicates.

8. **Documentation accuracy + WHY comments.** Every new file's header / docstring should describe its actual current state, not its planned future state. Every WHY comment should explain a non-obvious *reason*, not restate WHAT the code does. Stale comments lie to readers; aggressively prune them.

9. **API surface review.** Are the exported names self-explanatory? Could a third-party caller use this without reading the implementation? Privatize anything not needed publicly.

## Acceptance

- Each DRY commits separately so the reviewer can verify the consolidation.
- File an issue for every cross-cutting refactor uncovered (don't fix in this pass; just track).
- The parent phase ticket cannot close until this cleanup is complete.

## Anti-patterns (zero tolerance)

- "These are slightly different so I'll keep them separate." — if 80% is shared, share 80%.
- "I'll DRY this when there's a third user." — DRY at two; the third never comes.
- "It's just a small duplication." — small duplications compound. Three bugs all in slightly different copies of the same logic is the canonical anti-pattern this pass exists to prevent.
- "The language doesn't quite fit, so I wrote my own thing." — usually means you didn't look hard enough at the language's existing constructs. Look again.
- "I'll add language-feature use later." — usually never happens. The duct-tape calcifies.
- Leaving stale comments. — every comment must be current; if it's not, fix it or delete it.
- Names like `do_thing_2`, `helper3`, `process`, `inner`. — every function name owes the reader an explanation of what it actually does.
